To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) decentralized training is a promising approach to enable on-device learning over wireless networks; (2) it is challenging to train a model in a decentralized fashion, as decentralized training often suffers generalization issues; and (3) consensus can be a solution to improve the generalization of decentralized learning.

(1) the generalization gap between decentralized training and centralized training is due to consensus issues, (2) the generalization performance of decentralized training can be significantly improved by reducing the consensus error, and (3) the generalization of decentralized training is improved with a smaller communication topology, a more balanced data partitioning, and a smaller model size
(1) decentralized training is more robust to label noise than centralized training and (2) decentralized training with consensus improves model performance.
